$comment: What a plugin file's own yonto-plugin header means, for both hosts. The value is the manifest JSON text the header yields — the slice exactly, whitespace and all, because the two hosts have to agree on the bytes and each one's JSON parser ignores the rest — or null when the file carries no header a host will read. See contracts/content-source-http.md's "What a plugin is".

cases.why: a BOM before it, which an editor adds unasked
it stops at the first terminator, so nothing after it is manifest
a comment that is not this one
a line comment, which does not open one
a BOM after a newline, which the two languages disagree about if left to their own idea of blank
more than one BOM, which an editor and a pipeline can each add
a C0 separator, blank to Kotlin and not to JS, so neither host may take it
a non-breaking space, blank to both languages and to neither host
